**Finding: compliant (no audit right against us).**

The agreement contains no audit, inspection or licence-verification right binding Sparkling. I checked:

- **§ 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — substantive use restrictions only (copying, sublicensing, reverse engineering), with no verification or reporting mechanic attached.
- **§ 20 (General Matters)** — only time-of-essence and notices.
- Full-text searches for *audit*, *inspect*, *verify*, *records*, *premises*, *access*, *remote* — the only hits are Garman's telephone support access **to** Sparkling (§ 10) and mutual confidentiality (§ 14, "accounting records for which access is obtained by the other party").

Because no audit right exists, there is nothing to constrain on frequency, notice, business hours, auditor independence, cost allocation or system access. That outcome is better than the playbook's preferred position and benefits us, so this is recorded as compliant with no redline. Worth noting for negotiation awareness only: if Garman later proposes a verification clause, we should insert the preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, Garman's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct system access).
